pr_title: OSSL_PARAM and BIGNUM; ensure at least one byte is allocated
pr_body:
A zero BIGNUM contains zero bytes, while OSSL_PARAMs with an INTEGER (or
UNSIGNED INTEGER) data type are expected to have at least one data byte
allocated, containing a zero.  This wasn't handled correctly.

Fixes #20011
pr_comments: @levitte is your understanding here that the BN_new() case is also broken.. i.e. it points to a block for this case, but the next parameter would then reuse this location? The BN_secure case just shows an additional problem of using NULL (if there is one param)..

Would other functions that potentially pass an alloc of zero to param_push() also be a problem
(such as OSSL_PARAM_BLD_push_octet_string() ?)

> @levitte is your understanding here that the BN_new() case is also broken.. i.e. it points to a block for this case, but the next parameter would then reuse this location? The BN_secure case just shows an additional problem of using NULL (if there is one param)..

The problem seems to be most visible with `BN_secure`, but that shouldn't matter...  a zero shouldn't become 0 bytes of OSSL_PARAM data, for *any* C number type

I can confirm that the fix in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20013/commits/716cb7931bf6ab3f9f984a9187dd7fe74bf9d4ff does fix the problem.

I wonder if the OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX functions should also be made save about invalid OSSL_PARAMs being passed to it. A bogus application could pass invalid OSSL_PARAMs to providers (e.g. via EVP_PKEY_fromdata() ). I guess the OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX functions should not cause any troubles (like address sanitizer findings) if an invalid param is passed to it. I guess passing a OSSL_PARAM to a getter function with data = NULL and/or data_size = 0 does not make any sense no matter what, and should lead to an error return and add an error to the error stack.

> I guess passing a OSSL_PARAM to a getter function with data = NULL and/or data_size = 0 does not make any sense no matter what, and should lead to an error return and add an error to the error stack.

Not quite right.  You can do that to query what the minimum data_size should be for a particular OSSL_PARAM key.  This is documented:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/4b65d79d7132d6e46bfb385a76082f6502ef617b/doc/man3/OSSL_PARAM.pod?plain=1#L113-L116

> Not quite right. You can do that to query what the minimum data_size should be for a particular OSSL_PARAM key. This is documented:

I know that. I did not say that an OSSL_PARAM can never have data = NULL. What I am saying is that when using with the OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX() functions it can not have data = NULL or data_size = 0. So the OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX() functions should check for that and produce an error return if so.
Gah!  For once, I mixed up get and set.  Right you are...

I added a couple of more commits that have the numeric `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()` check that the `data` field is non-NULL and that the `data_size` field is non-zero, and also to have `OSSL_PARAM_set_BN()` ensure that there will be at least one byte of data.

That should satisfy what @ifranzki added on

> I added a couple of more commits that have the numeric OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX() check that the data field is non-NULL and that the data_size field is non-zero.

Don't you also need to add the check to `general_get_int()` and `general_get_uint()`? They are called by the `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()` functions if the size is not as expected.

Within `general_get_[u]int()` functions `[un]signed_from_[un]signed()` are called and there the `is_negative()` function is called on the `src` which is `p->data` and `p->data_size` which can be NULL. This would produce a segfault as far as I can tell.

> > I added a couple of more commits that have the numeric OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX() check that the data field is non-NULL and that the data_size field is non-zero.
> 
> Don't you also need to add the check to `general_get_int()` and `general_get_uint()`? They are called by the `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()` functions if the size is not as expected.

I don't understand...  if we have the checks early in `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()`, why would I have to reproduce the same checks in `general_get_int()` and `general_get_uint()`?

> > > I added a couple of more commits that have the numeric OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX() check that the data field is non-NULL and that the data_size field is non-zero.
> > 
> > 
> > Don't you also need to add the check to `general_get_int()` and `general_get_uint()`? They are called by the `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()` functions if the size is not as expected.
> 
> I don't understand... if we have the checks early in `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()`, why would I have to reproduce the same checks in `general_get_int()` and `general_get_uint()`?

You added the check to `OSSL_PARAM_get_int32()` etc, but not to `OSSL_PARAM_get_int()` etc. Within `OSSL_PARAM_get_int()` it calls `general_get_int()`. So no check before it reaches `general_get_int()`. 

This applies to `OSSL_PARAM_get_int()`, `OSSL_PARAM_get_long()`, `OSSL_PARAM_get_time_t()`, `OSSL_PARAM_get_uint()`, `OSSL_PARAM_get_size_t()`, `OSSL_PARAM_get_ulong()`.

The "Provider old versions compat / fips-provider-validation" CI fails...  it appears that the added checks in `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()` may break any provider that happens to set `data = NULL` and `data_size = 0` for a zero BN.

That's not promising.  We may have to forego that part of this PR, sadly enough.
The commit that changed the numeric `OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX()` functions is now gone.  I've made a separate draft PR, #20017, for those.
This pull request is ready to merge

Merged

issue_context.title: OSSL_PARAM_BLD_push_BN of zero secure BIGNUM leads to an OSSL_PARAM with data=NULL and data_size=0
comments: Allocating 1 byte is the fix I thought of while reading your great description.
This sounds like an error case to me, not a silent pass..
I agree with the 1 byte idea.
This hides the actual problem, which was unintentionally not setting the BIGNUM.

> This hides the actual problem, which was unintentionally not setting the BIGNUM.

Well, not quite.  A new BIGNUM is always a zero.  There's not such thing, conceptually speaking, as an unset BIGNUM.

What if a zero was intentional?  In that case, the issue presented here would still be a bug, would it not?

Besides, we push a positive amount of bytes (more than one, incidently) with all other numeric types, even when the value is zero, so pushing nothing for BIGNUMs specifically is inconsistent.

I was referring to this comment..
````It turned out that the OSSL_PARAM created via OSSL_PARAM_BLD_to_param() has data = NULL and data_size = 0.````

Interestingly enough, if you have other secure params, the `data` OSSL_PARAM field will not be NULL (`data_size` will still be zero).  That should work transparently (`bin2bn` will simply not read any bytes at all from the input pointer).

This bug turns out to be more subtle than I expected...

(I see what you mean after running the code locally)..
Just doing bn = BN_new() behaves differently from bn = BN_secure_new() (The secure case does set NULL, 0)
@ifranzki, would you mind testing your provider against an OpenSSL that's patched with #20013?

@levitte Yes, the fix in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20013 does fix the problem (its still unintended to pass a zero BIGNIM at all, but that's something I need to fix in my provider myself). 

I wonder if the OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX functions should also be made save about invalid OSSL_PARAMs being passed to it. A bogus application could pass invalid OSSL_PARAMs to providers (e.g. via EVP_PKEY_fromdata() ). I guess the OSSL_PARAM_get_XXX functions should not cause any troubles (like address sanitizer findings) if an invalid param is passed to it. I guess passing a OSSL_PARAM to a getter function with `data = NULL` and/or `data_size = 0` does not make any sense no matter what, and should lead to an error return and add an error to the error stack.
